final_content.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Define the *derived $I$-adic completion* of $K\in D(A)$ by $K^\wedge=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r),K)$, with its natural unit $K\to K^\wedge$. Let $D_{\rm comp}(A,I)$ be the full subcategory of derived $I$-complete complexes, i.e. those for which this unit is an isomorphism (equivalently $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_{f_i},K)=0$ for all $i$). These definitions use the derived Čech model and do not assume $A$ Noetherian or identify derived completion automatically with the naive inverse limit for arbitrary $K$. Then the restrictions
\[
R\Gamma_Z:D_{\rm comp}(A,I)\longrightarrow D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(-)^\wedge:D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\longrightarrow D_{\rm comp}(A,I)
\]
are quasi-inverse exact equivalences of triangulated categories. More precisely $R\Gamma_Z(K^\wedge)\simeq R\Gamma_Z(K)$ and $(R\Gamma_ZK)^\wedge\simeq K^\wedge$ for any $K\in D(A)$. This is the derived torsion-completion equivalence, not classical equality of torsion and complete modules.
hypotheses: A arbitrary, I finitely generated, derived torsion and completion via augmented Čech.
conclusions: Derived local cohomology and derived completion are quasi-inverse between torsion and complete subcategories.

semantic_review_note: Derived local cohomology and derived I-completion restrict to mutually quasi-inverse functors between derived torsion and derived complete subcategories for finitely generated I. The draft correctly uses Čech tensor/Hom rather than naive completion and preserves arbitrary commutative A.
